$comment: Machine-readable half of content/MANIFEST.md — the prose there explains WHY,
this file is what tools/assets/check-assets-present.mjs actually reads.
Keep the two in step; the prose is the source of truth for provenance, this
is the source of truth for paths and states.
state:  ready   = published to the R2 bucket; a build MUST find it (checked)
staged  = bytes exist locally, not yet published (checked with --staged)
planned = does not exist yet; nothing to check
retired = shipped once and no longer: never fetched, never checked, kept as history
licence: KEEP    = first-party, safe to publish
CONFIRM = provenance unresolved, must be settled before public launch
REPLACE = third-party or derivative; must be re-made before it ships

assets.notes: The hero asset. One MeshFilter/MeshRenderer, one flat material, per-vertex COLOR_0, 2764 verts. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (DEV-111): this note said both were LICENCE-BLOCKED and that was wrong, and it is the reason the JumpSeat still has no mesh. What is blocked is their two MATERIALS - DarkGrey from a vendor pack on the seat/console/button, OrangeSmooth from Unity SampleScenes (Unity Companion License, engine-locked) on the shell. DONE 2026-09-15 (DEV-114): the JumpSeat's meshes ship as ship.jumpseat.body / .shell / .strut below, and the stand-in is gone. Re-exported 2026-09-09 by tools/assets/convert-fbx.py at the correct unit scale (6.82 m, was 0.068 m) with COLOR_0.a forced to 1. RE-EXPORTED 2026-09-23 (DEV-328): wound OUTWARD, as the FBX is — every GLB this converter made from 2026-09-10 until then was inside-out (negative signed volume, masked by glTF doubleSided), because Blender 5.1 reverses the winding on a negative-scale apply and the converter reversed it again. assets.notes: 2016's HUD face (DEV-362 follow-up; Matt, 2026-09-24: "if you can - grab that old font"). Third-party and OPEN, not first-party: Typeface (C) Felipe Munoz 2014, CC BY-SA 4.0, stated in the font's own name table (IDs 0, 8, 9, 13, 14) and in `CC-BY-SA License.rtf` beside it in the Unity project. KEEP in this manifest's sense (safe to publish), on the terms the CC0 soundtrack rows use it for, with two duties those do not carry: ATTRIBUTION, which is README.md's credits and the notice file beside it (`font.crystal.licence`), and SHARE-ALIKE, which binds only a modified copy of the font — so it ships UNMODIFIED and must stay so. Loaded with the FontFace API by `render/hud-font.ts` for the dash readout (both editions) and the JumpSeat's fuel dome; the canvases fall back to the old stack if it fails. Binary, so never in git (the denylist); it lives only in the bucket.

assets.source: Written for this port (DEV-362 follow-up), from the font name table and the Unity project's CC-BY-SA License.rtf
assets.notes: The attribution CC BY-SA 4.0 asks for, served BESIDE the font so anyone who takes the file from the bucket takes the credit with it: author, title, the licence and its URL, and the statement that the font is unmodified (with its size and sha256). LF line endings, so its hash is the same on every host. The same credit is in README.md.

assets.notes: The rowing boat of the life pass (DEV-447). A bought Asset Store pack the shipped game already draws from (Simonet's live palms are its GL-Palmtree-03); 2016 bought this boat and placed it only in the pack's own example scene. Licensed for use: ships from R2, NEVER in git (hard rule 7). Binary FBX 6100 through convert-fbx.py's wm.fbx_import path and orient_prop, the rotation calibrated on this same pack's GL-Palmtree-01 twin. COLOR_0 is one colour per FACE: the atlas texel under each polygon's UV centroid, sRGB-decoded, times the material's linear _Color — 2016 rendered in Linear (m_ActiveColorSpace 1), so that is the albedo it would have shaded. No UVs, no texture. 3.168 x 1.132 x 1.226 m (x long), keel at y 0, positive signed volume. Written straight to public/ by `node tools/assets/convert-life.mjs` (read-only on $FF2_LEGACY); `--check` proves the bytes reproduce. Drawn by src/render/life-boats.ts.

The leaping dolphin of the life pass (DEV-449). Matt's own low-poly model from his polyfish game: first-party, safe to publish (a binary, so the bucket, not git). Skinned in polyfish; `node tools/assets/convert-life.mjs` bakes the rig's REST pose with three's own getVertexPosition (bind matrices and bones), one colour a face = vertex colour x the material's linear colour, the Color32 alpha dropped. 84 triangles, polyfish's units (0.0549 x 0.0479 x 0.1725; the preset scales it), nose +z / tail -z, refused unless the rig's own tail bone is behind the origin; 84 of 84 faces agree with the file's normals. `--check` reproduces the bytes. Drawn by src/render/life-leapers.ts.
